title: FedEDA: Federated Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning in EDA
problem: EDA ML models require large circuit benchmarks for training, but intellectual property security concerns prevent companies from sharing raw circuit data, creating data scarcity that limits progress in ML-driven EDA.
motivation: Advanced-node PPA optimization is increasingly complex and requires ML models to improve productivity, but IP protection conflicts with data sharing, creating a bottleneck in EDA research and tool development.
method: FedEDA enables teams to train a shared machine learning model for circuit design without revealing their proprietary designs—instead, they share only trained model weights (numerical patterns the model learned from data). The algorithm uses Rent's Rule, which describes how circuit connections scale with size, to capture the hierarchical structure of circuit data; this lets the system fairly combine everyone's trained weights even when participants have different amounts of training data.
key_novelty: FedEDA is the first federated learning algorithm for EDA that uses Rent's Rule to encode circuit hierarchy, enabling collaborative training of models for routability, RC parasitic, and wirelength prediction without sharing proprietary circuit designs.
contributions: FedEDA: first FL aggregation algorithm designed specifically for EDA tasks.
Rent's Rule and circuit size incorporation to capture hierarchical structure for better weight aggregation.
Outperforms existing FL algorithms on routability, parasitic RC, and wirelength prediction tasks.

metrics.other: outperforms existing FL algorithms on EDA tasks
